items.prompt: White to move. The knight on b4 and the bishop on f5 attack c2. Find a sound move.
hints: Count what attacks c2 and what guards it before you move a pawn.
A pawn move from c2 would leave the square empty. Which moves keep c2 guarded or block an attacker?
Look at Bb5+, Na3 or Bd3.
items.explain: c2 is attacked twice and defended once. Bb5+ gives check first, Na3 adds a second defender of c2, and Bd3 blocks the bishop's diagonal and offers a trade. The pawn move c3 looks like it attacks the knight but empties c2, which the next board shows.

claims.statement: Black has two attackers on c2.
White has one defender of c2.
At depth 16 Bb5+, Na3 and Bd3 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 the pawn move c3 is rated at least 3 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.c2c3: c3 attacks the knight but empties c2. At depth 16 it is rated at least 3 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight on b4 attacks your queen. Is there a move that wins material?
hints: Before you retreat, ask: can the queen do something forcing?
The queen can give check. Where would the check also attack something?
Look at b5.
items.explain: The queen does not have to retreat: Qb5+ gives check and attacks the knight, which nothing guards. Black loses material however the check is met: a block with ...Nfd7 loses the knight, and ...Nc6 loses the b7 pawn and more at depth 16.

claims.statement: Nothing of Black's defends the knight on b4.
At depth 16 Qb5+ is the engine's best move.
At depth 16 the retreat Qb3 is rated at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.d3b3: The retreat keeps the queen safe but misses the check. At depth 16 it is rated at least 1.5 pawns worse than Qb5+.

items.prompt: White to move. Count the attackers of c7 that you can bring, and the defenders. Find the strongest move.
hints: The bishop on f4 aims at c7. Which other piece can aim at the same square?
The knight on c3 can jump to a square that attacks c7.
Look at b5.
items.explain: c7 is protected only by the queen, and the knight jump to b5 brings a second attacker. At depth 16 the engine rates Nb5 far above any other move.

claims.statement: White already has one attacker of c7 (the bishop on f4).
At depth 16 Nb5 is the engine's best move, ahead of every other move by more than 1 pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's bishop pins the knight on f3. In our online data 45 White players here played the bishop to d3. Find a move the engine rates well.
hints: The bishop on f4 and the knight on f3 are both involved. What does ...e5 do to them?
Several moves are fine; one natural developing move is not. Which move walks into the break?
Look at Be2, Bg3, Bb5, h3 or Nc3.
items.explain: Black threatens the pawn break ...e5, which attacks the bishop while the knight is pinned. Be2 puts a piece behind the knight so the pin no longer costs the queen, Bg3 takes the bishop off the target square, and Bb5, h3 and Nc3 are within 0.65 pawn of the best. Bd3 develops but ignores the break, and at depth 16 it is rated at least 2 pawns worse than the best move.

claims.statement: The bishop on g4 attacks the knight on f3.
At depth 16 Be2, Bg3, Bb5, h3 and Nc3 are within 0.65 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 Bd3 is rated at least 2 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.f1d3: Bd3 ignores ...e5. At depth 16 it is rated at least 2 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight can take the pawn on d4. In our online data 172 of the 5,313 games that reached this position went that way. Is it a free pawn?
hints: Count: one attacker, one defender. Now compare their values.
The knight is worth more than a pawn. Who recaptures?
The capture loses material.
items.explain: Equal numbers are not enough: the capturer is a knight and the defender is the queen, but nothing guards the knight, so the queen simply takes it. Count the attackers and defenders, then look at what is left on the square.

claims.statement: Black has one attacker of d4.
White has one defender of d4.
Along the engine's best defence Black ends at least a pawn down in material after the capture.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.
hints: What does your opponent's last move leave undefended?
Check each enemy piece: is any attacked and unguarded?
One piece can be taken for free.
items.explain: The pawn move to e3 opened the diagonal from d1 to g4, and the bishop has no defender. Bishops that go to g4 before the knight stands on f3 can be taken by the queen.

claims.statement: Black's bishop on g4 is loose (attacked by the queen, defended by nothing).
The queen takes the bishop and, along the engine's best defence, White ends at least 2 points of material ahead.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.
hints: What does your opponent's last move attack?
Is the attacked pawn defended by anything?
Defend it with a pawn or a piece.
items.explain: The knight attacks d5 and the pawn is unguarded. Defending it with a pawn or a knight keeps the position playable; the greedy queen move loses.

claims.statement: At depth 16 e6 and Nf6 are within 0.2 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 taking the pawn on b2 is rated at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.b6b2: Taking b2 leaves d5 hanging. At depth 16 it is rated at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.
hints: Which of your pawns could become a target after your next move?
Count the attackers of c7 now, and the pieces that could join them.
Take away the square from which a knight would attack: a6 does that.
items.explain: The developing move Nc6 leaves c7 guarded only by the queen against Bf4 and a knight jump to b5. Several moves are within half a pawn of the best: a6 takes b5 away from the knight, and c4, Bd7, Be7, Bd6, cxd4 and Qa5 are also fine.

claims.statement: At depth 16 a6, c4, Bd7, Be7, Bd6, cxd4 and Qa5 are within half a pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 the knight move Nc6 is rated at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.b8c6: Nc6 leaves c7 to the queen alone. At depth 16 it is rated at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.
hints: What does your opponent's last move attack or prepare?
Which of your pieces could be hit with check next move?
A quiet developing move is enough.
items.explain: Nb4 attacks the queen but loses the knight to a check on b5. Several quiet moves are within 0.3 pawn of the best, e6 among them.

claims.statement: At depth 16 e6, h6, Qd7, a6 and Nh5 are within 0.3 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 the knight move Nb4 is rated at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.c6b4: The queen answers with Qb5+ and takes the knight. At depth 16 Nb4 is rated at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.
hints: What does your opponent's last move attack or prepare?
Count the attackers of each of your pawns.
Nothing is loose here: a developing move is fine.
items.explain: Nothing is loose and no trap is set. The a-pawn already covers b5, so the knight jump that hurt c7 in the other position does not work here, and Nc6 is fine. The habit is to ask the three questions and sometimes find that the answers are quiet.

claims.statement: At depth 16 b5, Nc6, Nbd7, b6, Bd6, Be7, Bd7, c4 and h6 are within 0.2 pawn of the engine's best move.
